Reconstruct a Triangular Mesh from a 3D Point Cloud

Source: R/createMesh.R
createMesh.Rd

Reconstructs a triangular surface from a 3D point cloud using linear binning and Marching Cubes, and returns the result as a mesh3d object.

Usage

createMesh(
  panel,
  resolNbin = c(4, 4, 2),
  meshCad = NULL,
  zeroBorder = FALSE,
  kFactor = NULL,
  truncFactor = 3.5,
  levelFactor = 0.99,
  coverageTol = 0.99
)

Arguments

panel

A numeric matrix or data frame with three columns containing the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the point cloud.

resolNbin

A numeric vector of length three defining the approximate binning resolution in the X, Y, and Z directions. Default is c(4, 4, 2).

meshCad

Optional mesh3d object used as a reference for the spatial coverage of the reconstructed surface. Default is NULL.

zeroBorder

Logical. If TRUE, adds a zero-valued layer around the X and Z limits before surface extraction. Default is FALSE.

kFactor

Numeric factor used to determine the tolerance for removing low-density nodes. If NULL, it is selected automatically. Default is NULL.

truncFactor

Numeric factor used to truncate high-density node weights. Default is 3.5.

levelFactor

Numeric factor used to define the isosurface extraction level. Default is 0.99.

coverageTol

Numeric value between 0 and 1 defining the minimum spatial coverage required relative to the reference bounding box. Default is 0.99.

Value

A list containing:

  • mesh: reconstructed surface as a mesh3d object.

  • bin: processed binning object.

  • contours: disconnected surfaces generated by Marching Cubes, ordered from largest to smallest.

  • params: parameters used during reconstruction.

Details

Linear binning is performed with npsp::binning() and the grid coordinates are obtained with npsp::coordvalues(). Low-density nodes are removed and high-density weights are truncated before extracting the isosurface with misc3d::contour3d().

When zeroBorder = TRUE, one zero-valued layer is added on both sides of the X and Z directions to facilitate surface closure.

If several disconnected surfaces are produced, they are ordered by size and progressively merged until the reconstructed surface reaches coverageTol times the dimensions of the reference bounding box.

See also

npsp::binning(), npsp::coordvalues(), misc3d::contour3d(), rgl::tmesh3d()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the theoretical CAD model
data("cad", package = "dimControl")

# Prepare the theoretical panel mesh
meshTeor <- preparePanelMesh(cad)

# Simulate panel points without floor points
panel <- simulatePanelFloorCloud(
  mesh = meshTeor,
  nPanel = 1e7,
  nFloor = 0,
  seed = 1
)

# Reconstruct the mesh from the panel point cloud
result <- createMesh(
  panel = panel,
  resolNbin = c(4, 4, 2),
  zeroBorder = TRUE
)

mesh <- result$mesh

# Display point cloud and reconstructed mesh side by side
rgl::clear3d()
rgl::mfrow3d(1, 2)

rgl::points3d(panel, col = "blue")
rgl::title3d("Panel point cloud", level = 4)

rgl::next3d()
rgl::shade3d(mesh, col = "lightgray")
rgl::title3d("Reconstructed mesh", level = 4)
} # }
